svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif
svg.title: The harness is a loom: tangled intent in, ordered work out
svg.desc: An overview of the whole system drawn as a loom. On the far left is the input: raw intent, listed as the forms it actually arrives in, which are a one-line idea, a meeting transcript, legacy documents, an existing repository, an empty repository, and half-written specifications. Loose multicoloured threads leave those blocks and tangle together as they travel right. They pass into spec-builder, which sits outside the harness and does one job: routing any input format into a single contract written to international standards. That contract enters the harness, labelled harness-bootstrap and drawn as a large frame. Inside the frame, rules and hooks come down from above into the agents at the centre. Rules carry conventions such as conventional commits and protecting secrets, and are scoped by path. Hooks fire before and after a tool call, and an exit code of 2 blocks the call. On the right of the frame is a rail of two panels at the same level. Skill Discovery scans this project's manifests to work out its tech stack and then finds the skills that match it, reading files such as requirements.txt, Gemfile, csproj, build.gradle and pnpm-workspace.yaml, as well as marketplace catalogs. Below it, Skill Wire connects a chosen skill to the agent seat that needs it, and nothing is installed unless the user chooses it. The rail feeds the skills, which feed the agents. The agents are the narrow waist of the loom where everything is woven together. Below the waist, three ordered outputs leave in a single colour, each with its own connection: documents with a graph, a plan of tasks with owners, and code with a graph. At the bottom of the frame sits state, holding the prompt, the run history and the task board, which the agents both read and write, and which survives compaction and restart. State is also what the harness viewer reads. The viewer sits below the frame and carries four functions: a flow and graph view of every wire, an assess function that scores the harness and names what is missing, a toggle that switches any rule or hook off, and a watch mode that re-scans as files change. No model is involved in any of it. The point of the picture is that chaos goes in and controlled, inspectable work comes out.
svg.text: Tangled intent goes in on the left. Ordered, inspectable work comes out. Everything between is the harness.
Nothing has to be tidy first.
one contract you and the AI share

of step with each other. Inside the
frame they drift in step, because
